newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds mixed in thin pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds mixed in thin pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds were mixed in thin late trading Wednesday, as the market eased into a long Easter weekend starting Thursday, dealers said.
"The market was a bit sapped by the holidays and so that explains why prices were sagging today," one dealer said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/8 at $90.5, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 edged up $0.05 to $126.9.

The market was still a bit groggy after a round of profit-taking which followed Tuesday's 25-basis points hike in the U.S. Federal Funds rate. International bonds were also undermined by strong U.S. durable goods indicators Wednesday.

"The market wasn't so fazed by the modification to U.S. rates as that was already priced in, but now there is a possibility of a new modification at the (U.S. Federal) Reserve's next meeting in May," another trader said.
